title: Muffin — Data coverage
description: How complete the data is and where the gaps are. From market.coverage_sample, a twice-daily snapshot of market.coverage_current — one definition, so the table can never disagree with the view.

panels.title: Funnel — the stages that genuinely gate each other
panels.description:
A REAL FUNNEL, over the five stages that are genuinely nested — each one REQUIRES the stage above it. Sector and industry are read off the profile response, and the profile needs a symbol, so the chain is causal rather than merely sorted.

The other facets are NOT in here on purpose. Measured 2026-08-28, `metrics` (8,948) EXCEEDS `statements` (8,842), because metrics also come straight from SEC XBRL rather than only from stored statements — so putting them in a funnel would assert a pipeline that does not exist. They are in the bar panel below, which claims no ordering.

Grafana OSS has no funnel panel; a horizontal bar gauge sorted descending is the honest equivalent and needs no plugin.

targets.rawSql:
select 'universe' as metric, sum(securities)::float as value   from market.coverage_sample
 where dimension = 'country_sector'
   and sampled_at = (select max(sampled_at) from market.coverage_sample)
   and security_type_code = 'equity'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',1) like '$country'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',2) like '$sector'
union all select 'symbol',   sum(with_symbol)::float     from market.coverage_sample
 where dimension = 'country_sector'
   and sampled_at = (select max(sampled_at) from market.coverage_sample)
   and security_type_code = 'equity'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',1) like '$country'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',2) like '$sector'
union all select 'profile',  sum(with_profile)::float    from market.coverage_sample
 where dimension = 'country_sector'
   and sampled_at = (select max(sampled_at) from market.coverage_sample)
   and security_type_code = 'equity'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',1) like '$country'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',2) like '$sector'
union all select 'sector',   sum(with_sector)::float     from market.coverage_sample
 where dimension = 'country_sector'
   and sampled_at = (select max(sampled_at) from market.coverage_sample)
   and security_type_code = 'equity'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',1) like '$country'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',2) like '$sector'
union all select 'industry', sum(with_industry)::float   from market.coverage_sample

   and security_type_code = 'equity'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',1) like '$country'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',2) like '$sector'

panels.title: Country × sector — completeness (sortable; worst first by default)
panels.description:
Every (country, sector) bucket holding at least 20 securities — 106 of the 637 combinations. Click a column to re-sort; the default is worst-first because that is where the work is.

IT USED TO BE `limit 60`, AND THAT HID THE UNITED STATES. US is the best-covered country, so its eleven real sectors ranked 90-98 of 106 and fell off the end — leaving only `US / unknown` (92 securities with no sector, genuinely 0%) visible, which read as 'the US is missing'. A worst-first list truncated at an arbitrary row silently deletes whatever is healthy, and the healthy things are the ones you check when something looks wrong.

The >=20 floor stays: a completeness figure over a handful of securities is noise, and a two-stock bucket at 0% would otherwise top the list for ever.

THE SIZE FLOOR IS A VARIABLE, NOT A CONSTANT. At the default of 20 it hides 531 of 637 buckets — a defensible choice (a 2-security bucket at 0% is noise, not a signal) but not one that should be invisible. Set `Min securities in bucket` to 1 to see all of them. The panel previously ALSO carried `limit 60`, which deleted the United States: 106 buckets cleared the floor, the US ranked 90-98 of them BECAUSE it is well covered, and the only US row that survived was `US / unknown` at 0%.

targets.rawSql:
select split_part(bucket,'|',1) as "country",
       split_part(bucket,'|',2) as "sector",
       securities,
       round(100.0*complete/nullif(securities,0),1) as "complete %",
       round(100.0*with_statements/nullif(securities,0),1) as "statements %",
       round(100.0*with_industry/nullif(securities,0),1)   as "industry %"
  from market.coverage_sample
 where dimension = 'country_sector'
   and sampled_at = (select max(sampled_at) from market.coverage_sample)
   and security_type_code = 'equity'
   and securities >= $minsize
   and split_part(bucket,'|',1) like '$country'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',2) like '$sector'
 order by 100.0*complete/nullif(securities,0) asc

panels.title: Is this scope improving?
panels.description: Completeness over time for the current selection. Coverage samples TWICE DAILY behind an 11-hour gate, so this needs days rather than hours to say anything — a flat line here after a deploy is youth, not a stall. `showPoints: always` because two samples a day is not a line.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time, 'complete' as metric,
       round(100.0*sum(complete)/nullif(sum(securities),0),1) as value
  from market.coverage_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and dimension='country_sector' and security_type_code='equity'
   and split_part(bucket,'|',1) like '$country' and split_part(bucket,'|',2) like '$sector'
 group by sampled_at order by sampled_at

panels.title: Breakdowns — every sampled dimension (WHOLE UNIVERSE, not filtered by the variables above)
Completeness now, by security type
panels.description:
Completeness per security type RIGHT NOW. A bond arrives from an N-PORT filing and that is all it will ever be, so `required_facet` decides what each type owes — which is why bonds read 100% and are not being compared against an equity's fifteen facets.

THIS PANEL COVERS THE WHOLE UNIVERSE and is NOT affected by the country/sector variables above. `coverage_sample` holds one bucket list per dimension, so there is no (cap band x country) cross to filter on — reading these as if they were scoped would be reading a number that is not what it says.

targets.rawSql: select security_type_code as metric, round(100.0*sum(complete)/nullif(sum(securities),0),1) as value from market.coverage_sample where sampled_at=(select max(sampled_at) from market.coverage_sample) and dimension='security_type' group by security_type_code order by 2 desc

panels.title: Completeness by security type
panels.description:
The same figure over time. ETFs read 0% because `required_facet` asks them for a `price` row and ETF returns are computed from `etf/historical` into `performance` — bars were never stored. That is a one-row fix in `required_facet`, not an ingestion failure.

THIS PANEL COVERS THE WHOLE UNIVERSE and is NOT affected by the country/sector variables above. `coverage_sample` holds one bucket list per dimension, so there is no (cap band x country) cross to filter on — reading these as if they were scoped would be reading a number that is not what it says.

targets.rawSql: select sampled_at as time, security_type_code as metric, round(100.0*complete/nullif(securities,0),1) as value from market.coverage_sample where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and dimension='security_type' order by sampled_at

panels.title: Equities with no sector at all
panels.description:
Equities that reach no sector. TYPED TO EQUITY ON PURPOSE: untyped, this bucket reads 16,401 — but 15,159 of those are BONDS, which arrive from an N-PORT filing and will never carry a sector. One flat definition reports most of the universe permanently broken for a facet that can never apply, and the number gets ignored within a week.

Should trend DOWN as security-industries and security-profiles drain. Flat with a non-zero value means a backlog is stalled, or is draining by MARKING rather than by working.

WHOLE UNIVERSE — not filtered by the country/sector variables above.

targets.rawSql: select sampled_at as time, sum(securities) filter (where bucket='unknown') as "no sector" from market.coverage_sample where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and dimension='sector' and security_type_code='equity' group by sampled_at order by sampled_at

panels.description:

It previously carried `limit 30`, the same defect that hid the United States from the cross table: a worst-first list truncated at an arbitrary row silently deletes whatever is healthy, and the healthy rows are the ones you go looking for when something seems wrong.

list.name: country
list.label: Country
list.query:
select distinct split_part(bucket,'|',1) as __text, split_part(bucket,'|',1) as __value
  from market.coverage_sample
 where dimension='country_sector'
   and sampled_at=(select max(sampled_at) from market.coverage_sample)

list.name: sector
list.label: Sector
list.query:
select distinct split_part(bucket,'|',2) as __text, split_part(bucket,'|',2) as __value
  from market.coverage_sample
 where dimension='country_sector'
   and sampled_at=(select max(sampled_at) from market.coverage_sample)

list.name: minsize
list.label: Min securities in bucket
list.description: Buckets smaller than this are hidden. A 2-security bucket at 0% would otherwise top a worst-first list. Set to 1 to see EVERY bucket — nothing is hidden by a decision you cannot see.
